source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: Entry2167 removes FindPrevUnread and performs the reverse scan in NavigateFromPos. It starts at the last row for an unset start index, otherwise at the previous row. After expanding a collapsed thread with unread children, it increases curIndex by numExpanded+1; the for-loop decrement then visits the last inserted child. It skips read and dummy rows and returns the selected row index/key. The index-controlled loop and mutation are part of this algorithm, not an interchangeable action-iteration style. Fixed source preserves the loop. The added folderD test collapses threads, starts from message9 and checks 8,7,3,0, then checks that another previous-unread command causes no extra selection/load during a 500ms observation. The reviewer explicitly requested this threaded fixture and accepted grouped-by-sort as an untested gap; search/grouped-by-sort coverage is not established by these selected assertions. Bug 1941139 comment2 remains missing, so zero complete-audit credit. No test, Try or native navigation was run.
title: Previous-unread navigation scans expanded children in reverse view order
